title: Solstia claims adapter — sticky notes
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Customer: Solstia Insurance (mid-size regional insurer).
- Goal: Replace a rules-heavy claims triage pipeline with an LLM-assisted claims adapter to: (1) extract structured fields from intake text/PDFs, (2) assign triage buckets and severity, and (3) surface recommended next-action snippets for agents.
- Want private deployment (VPC) and ability to optionally run on-prem for high-sensitivity workflows.
- Main ask: <200ms p50 inference for short extraction calls (~150–400 tokens), p95 <600ms.

Attendees (2025-11-04 kickoff):
- Marcus Chen (Redwood SE) — owner
- Elena Park (Redwood Solutions) — prompts + evals
- Renee Ortiz (Solstia, Eng Manager) — integration lead
- Tomás Ruiz (Solstia, Data Platform) — infra / security
- Janet Wu (Solstia, Claims SME) — rules mapping

High-level nonfunctional constraints (from Tomás):
- VPC peering preferred; no public egress for PHI-containing claims.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) mandatory for Private.
- Audit logs retained 7 years; RL logging path must be configurable (redact PII).
- Compliance: must support in-region deployment (EU/US depending on customer segment).

Functional scope (MVP):
- Input: free-text claim notes + OCR’d PDF text (we’ll accept plain text payloads).
- Output: JSON with fields {claim_id, claimant_name_masked, date_of_loss, severity_level, triage_bucket, recommended_action, confidence_score}.
- Also return short human-facing summary (1–2 lines).
- Single-call inference per claim (no multi-turn conversational state).

Performance notes / gotchas observed in quick tests:
- Tokenization blowups for OCR'd PDFs: lots of weird unicode/line-breaks cause much larger token counts. Need precleaning step. (Elena: propose light regex normalize + whitespace collapse on client side.)
- Cold-start P95 spikes when switching model variants (FP16 -> int8 quantized). Recommend warm pools for dedicated capacity.
- Long-running KV cache not relevant (single-call) but we get latency wins from batching for embedding-based similarity checks. However batch adds latency; recommend separate asynchronous batch pipeline for similarity enrichment vs inline request.
- Idempotency for retries: must include client request id to avoid duplicate billing/duplicate writes to claims DB.
- Rate-limits: Solstia expects bursty traffic during business hours (8am–10am local peaks). We should advise burst capacity + backlog window to smooth.

Model & serving decisions (notes):
- Start with a smaller open model (e.g., redwood-compact-1) for extraction -> deterministic outputs + lower token costs. Use a constrained prompt + schema enforcement.
- Have fallback to a larger model (redwood-large-2) for low-confidence cases (confidence_score < 0.7) or when certain fields can’t be parsed.
- Use Redwood Optimize recommendations: quantize to int8 for Dedicated pools to reduce cost; keep 1–2 warm workers per pool for steady p50.

Prompting sketch (for Elena to iterate):
- System: "You are a claims extraction assistant. Given an input claim note, return only valid JSON with the following keys: claim_id, date_of_loss (YYYY-MM-DD or blank), severity_level (low/med/high), triage_bucket (routing tag), recommended_action (1-sentence), confidence_score (0-1). Mask any PII in recommended_action."
- User (example): "[OCR TEXT]" -> expect quick structured JSON.

Integration/infra checklist (Tomás):
- [ ] VPC Peering + route table updated (security team).
- [ ] KMS integration tested in staging (customer-managed).
- [ ] Logging + audit sink to Solstia S3 bucket (redaction rules applied).
- [ ] Network egress rules: no external endpoints allowed except Redwood private endpoint over peered VPC.
- [ ] SLO monitor dashboards + tracer tags (route:solstia-claims-adapter).

Edge cases / unresolved questions
- OCR quality pipeline: who owns pre-clean? Solstia prefers to keep OCR in-house (makes sense) but wants Redwood to accept noisy text. We should document pre-clean suggestions and provide a tiny client sanitizer snippet.
- PII redaction: Redwood must support server-side redaction before logs leave customer VPC; confirm our Private agent supports configurable scrub rules (Tomás to validate).
- Cost allocation: Solstia wants per-team billing across business lines; need to expose per-route token metrics at token-level cost. Match to their internal chargeback tags.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
- Marcus: Draft integration runbook + sample request/response (by 2025-11-10).
- Elena: Write 6 prompt templates and 30 eval examples from historical claims (by 2025-11-12).
- Tomás: Confirm KMS + VPC peering feasibility with infra/security and share network checklist (by 2025-11-07).
- Renee: Provide 50 representative OCR outputs (anonymized) and claim mapping table (by 2025-11-14).
- Joint: Quick staging demo (redwood-hosted private deployment) scheduled w/c 2025-11-18.

Action items for demo prep (short):
- Build schema-enforcement wrapper that validates LLM JSON and returns deterministic fallbacks (Marcus + Elena).
- Add a preflight sanitizer script (Tomás) that: removes weird unicode, normalizes dashes, collapses repeated whitespace, strips long base64 blobs.
- Create sample mapping file from rules -> triage buckets (Janet to supply).

Quick risk notes for sales/legal
- If Solstia requires guaranteed p95 < 400ms we need dedicated reserved capacity commitment; otherwise recommend best-effort SLA for MVP.
- Audit log retention 7 years could increase storage costs; flag in contract.

Misc snippets (copyable):
- Minimal request example:
POST /v1/claims/adapt
Headers: {Authorization: Bearer <key>, Idempotency-Key: <uuid>}
Body: {"text":"<OCR text>","claim_id":"CL-1234","region":"us-east-1"}

- Minimal response example:
{
  "claim_id":"CL-1234",
  "date_of_loss":"2025-11-01",
  "severity_level":"med",
  "triage_bucket":"medical-review",
  "recommended_action":"Request claimant photo of damage + schedule nurse review.",
  "confidence_score":0.82
}

Notes-to-self: keep demo focused on 3 things: clean extraction, deterministic schema, and clear fallback path. Avoid showing large-model hallucination examples unless we can quantify improvement with eval set.

---
End sticky notes.
